headline: 7 Claude Prompt Habits to Unlearn (Anthropic Guide)
summary: Prompting habits inherited from other LLMs degrade Claude's reasoning. Adopting Anthropic's structural prompt patterns unlocks deterministic, high-accuracy outputs.

slides.title: 7 Claude Prompt Habits to Unlearn Today
slides.subtitle: Why standard LLM prompting habits degrade Claude's intelligence
slides.body: Copy-pasting prompts designed for other LLMs into Claude leads to degraded reasoning. Anthropic designed Claude around distinct structural parsing principles.
slides.deep_dive: Most engineers treat LLMs identically. But Claude parses hierarchy, instructions, and context differently, demanding structured wrappers over conversational chatter.
slides.key_fact: Claude relies on structural tags rather than conversational markdown cues.
slides.why_it_matters: Eliminates hallucination and drastically boosts prompt determinism.

slides.title: The Structured Blueprint Model
slides.subtitle: Think of Claude as an architectural blueprint scanner
slides.body: Claude operates like a blueprint scanner. It isolates instructions, data, and context into clear semantic compartments rather than reading a flat script.

steps.title: Isolate Context
steps.desc: Wrap raw reference material inside explicit semantic boundary tags.

steps.title: Assign Directives
steps.desc: Position rules and core questions after reference context for maximum focus.

steps.title: Prime Generation
steps.desc: Direct the response channel by prefilling the assistant turn directly.

slides.title: The Structural Parsing Pipeline
slides.subtitle: How structured token boundaries eliminate prompt ambiguity
slides.body: Claude resolves instructions faster when input documents, background knowledge, and expected responses are partitioned into independent semantic regions.
slides.input: Reference documents and user queries isolated inside distinct structural envelopes.
slides.processing: Attention layers cleanly separate reference tokens from operational instructions.
slides.output: Deterministic, format-compliant responses without conversational preamble or context bleed.

slides.title: Flat Prompts vs. Structural Tagging
slides.subtitle: Comparing legacy prompting habits with Anthropic native design
slides.body: Moving to structural prompting trades minimal setup overhead for zero ambiguity and tighter schema compliance.
left_items: Instructions blend directly into reference text
Higher token confusion during long context retrieval
Vulnerable to unintended prompt injection risks
right_items: Eliminates context bleeding across multiple documents
Guarantees deterministic JSON and schema generation

slides.title: Negative Prompts & Empty Prefills
slides.subtitle: Telling Claude what NOT to do instead of framing boundaries
slides.body: Engineers often list negative restrictions or forget prefilling the assistant turn, causing Claude to ramble before answering.
slides.mistake_desc: Stacking negative rules like 'Do not do this' and leaving the assistant response channel unguided.
slides.fix_desc: Define explicit positive outcomes and prime the first output token inside the assistant turn.

slides.title: High-Volume Document Pipelines
slides.subtitle: How enterprise systems leverage structured boundaries
slides.body: Enterprise data pipelines use prefilled responses and tagged boundaries to parse complex financial filings without post-processing failures.
slides.challenge: Legacy markdown prompts produced inconsistent JSON formats and conversational chatter across long documents.
slides.solution: Engineers wrapped documents in semantic boundary tags and prefilled the opening brace.
slides.impact: Eliminated downstream schema failures and removed preamble text across production workloads.

slides.title: Claude Optimization Checklist
slides.subtitle: Essential habits to audit across your AI engineering pipelines
slides.body: Audit your prompts with these four fundamental rules recommended directly by Anthropic engineering.
items: Partition prompt components using explicit structural boundary tags
Place reference context above operational instructions in prompt flow
Prefill the assistant response turn to lock down output formats
Replace negative restrictions with clear positive behavioural targets

slides.title: Master Modern Claude Architecture
slides.subtitle: Shift from conversational chatting to structural engineering
slides.body: Claude excels when treated as a compiler of structured information rather than an open-ended conversational partner.
takeaways: Use structural envelopes to prevent context bleeding across inputs
Prefill assistant responses to guarantee strict schema adherence
Position task instructions after context to sharpen attention focus
